about.title: About Gear Ratio Calculator
about.description: Our Gear Ratio Calculator helps you determine ring and pinion ratios for drivetrain planning, axle swaps, off-road builds, and workshop-style reference checks. Gear ratio affects acceleration, cruising RPM, fuel economy, towing ability, and overall drivability. With this gear ratio calculator, you can test multiple ring and pinion combinations and see how each setup changes the final drive ratio.

faq.q: What is a gear ratio and why does it matter?
faq.a: Gear ratio equals ring gear teeth divided by pinion gear teeth (e.g., 41 ÷ 11 = 3.73). Higher numerical ratios improve acceleration by multiplying torque but raise cruising RPM; lower ratios reduce RPM at speed and improve fuel efficiency. Our gear ratio calculator helps you compare these tradeoffs.

faq.q: How do I calculate ring and pinion gear ratio?
faq.a: Simply divide the ring gear tooth count by the pinion gear tooth count. For example, 41 ring teeth ÷ 11 pinion teeth = 3.73 ratio. Our calculator performs this calculation and displays results for easy comparison.

faq.q: How do larger tires affect gear ratio choice for off-road builds?
faq.a: Larger tires effectively reduce torque multiplication, so off-road builds typically use higher numerical axle ratios (4.10–4.88) to restore drivability and keep the engine closer to its intended operating range. Use our calculator to compare ratios for your tire size.

faq.q: Does a higher gear ratio hurt highway fuel economy?
faq.a: Higher numerical ratios increase engine RPM at highway speeds, which typically increases fuel consumption and noise. Choose a gear ratio that balances your needs for acceleration, towing capability, and cruising comfort based on your primary driving conditions.

faq.q: Do I need to re-gear both axles on a 4WD vehicle?
faq.a: Yes, front and rear axle ratios must match exactly to prevent driveline binding when in 4WD mode. Always re-gear both axles to the same ratio. Mismatched ratios can cause expensive drivetrain damage.

faq.q: What are common gear ratios for different applications?
faq.a: Street performance: 3.73-4.10, Off-road/towing: 4.10-4.88, Highway cruising: 3.08-3.42, Drag racing: 4.30-4.88. The right ratio depends on your engine's power band, tire size, transmission ratios, and intended use.
